A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FS-Researcher. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison. V2 retains Appendices A-H and adds Appendices I-M.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark evaluations, module ablations, scaling experiments, cost measurements and case analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds BrowseComp evaluation, Gemini experiments and the original analyses in Appendices I-M.

M1.justification: The core dual-agent workflow and persistent workspace remain unchanged. V2 introduces tested variants using GPT-5-mini to summarize webpages before retaining them in context (Appendix L) and adding report rephrasing (Appendix K). Rephrasing is explicitly excluded from the default framework.

E1.justification: V2 adds BrowseComp to the retained DeepResearch Bench and DeepConsult evaluations. This substantially extends task coverage from open-ended report generation to information seeking with verifiable answers, using 100 sampled BrowseComp questions.

E2.justification: The original benchmark comparator rosters remain intact. V2 adds a search-only Gemini-2.5-Pro comparator in Appendix I and comparisons against official Claude-Sonnet-4.5 and GPT-5 harnesses on BrowseComp. Gemini versions of FS-Researcher are additional proposed-system configurations, not new baselines.

E3.justification: V2 substantially expands evaluation design through BrowseComp answer accuracy on 100 of 1,266 questions, Gemini backbone experiments, and GPT-5-mini with 10 rounds on the existing 10-query sample. It also introduces 10-round rephrasing, 3-round compression and runtime-profiling conditions. Previously stated protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendices I-M investigate harness contributions, smaller-model usability, readability recovery, compression-related cost reduction and file-I/O overhead. These substantially extend the analytical evidence beyond the retained module ablations, scaling analysis, tool-use analysis and case study.

E5.justification: Both versions state that scores average three test runs and retain the same judging-aggregation description in Appendix C. V2 introduces no new seed reporting, uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: Existing result values are retained, while substantial new results appear: Gemini FS-Researcher scores 52.51 RACE and 74.88% DeepConsult wins; BrowseComp accuracies are 55.0% with Claude and 68.0% with GPT-5. Appendices I-M add harness, smaller-model, rephrasing, compression and latency results, including Context Builder cost reduction from $3.77 to $2.00.

T1.justification: The ReAct workflow equations and Appendix C scoring definitions are unchanged. V2's statements about readability and comprehensiveness being orthogonal are conceptual interpretations, not new formal definitions, proofs or theoretical results.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central framework and test-time-scaling claims. V2 adds negligible file-I/O latency as an introductory claim and extends its experimental generalization claim to answer-verifiable information seeking in Section 3.2.

C2.justification: V1 tentatively attributes reduced readability to larger or redundant contexts; v2 describes it as a recoverable writing-style artifact. V2 also qualifies the strong-model dependency limitation using GPT-5-mini results, acknowledges that its rephrasing prompt is benchmark-specific, and adds substantive interpretations of harness contributions, compression compatibility and latency tradeoffs.

D1.justification: V2 supplies the rephrasing instruction, identifies GPT-5-mini as the webpage summarizer, explains summary-only context retention, and reports additional API-cost and stage-level runtime information. Existing tool descriptions, checklists and code/data access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 5 and the reference list remain unchanged. Appendix L nevertheless extends research positioning by explicitly presenting FS-Researcher as complementary to existing context-compression methods, whereas the earlier discussion primarily emphasized their limitations.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized explanatory and interpretive revisions, clarifies the session-budget terminology, adds acknowledgments and a Project Lead credit, and appends Sections I-M. The main narrative structure and most existing prose remain intact; this is not an extensive rewrite.

P2.justification: V2 substantially expands tabular presentation with BrowseComp Table 4 and analysis Tables 11-15, several reusing existing results as controls. Tables 2-3 gain Gemini rows. Existing figures are retained, while older tables are renumbered and reflowed, including bringing the two scaling-data tables together.

improvement.justification: The added same-backbone controls and cost/rephrasing experiments strengthen empirical support and clarify practical tradeoffs. Benefits are limited by sparse BrowseComp protocol details and stronger readability interpretations without uncertainty estimates. A new latency statement also overreaches: Table 15 implies about 0.049% file-I/O time for Report Writing, although combined runtime supports the claimed below-0.03% figure. Overall, the additions provide a useful but limited net improvement.
